title: Compute Ledger, version 1.0.0, with changes to 20 November 2026 (the latest tables)
description: Public records on the footprint of AI compute, with what companies and governments say kept apart (the column side). Start with the table measurements.

measurements.description: Every figure in the ledger, one row each: permits, metered loads, filed demand, company statements, computed values. Start here.

columns.measurement_id: Content hash of feed, subject, metric, metric_detail, period, value_as_published, source_url, side and entry_id. It changes when any of those change (a corrected figure gets a new id); see CHANGELOG.md.
columns.subject_type: What the figure is about: a site (site_register), an entity such as a utility (entity_register), or a ledger entry as a whole (entries).
columns.subject_id: The site_id, entity_id or entry id.
columns.entry_id: The ledger entry the figure belongs to, if any.
columns.metric: What is measured, from pipeline/measurement_vocab.json (e.g. electricity_consumed, permitted_standby_generation).
columns.metric_detail: What exactly the figure counts, in words: scope, fuel, building, part of the site.
columns.value: The figure in its published unit (the low end for a range).
columns.value_high: The high end of a range, if the source gives one.
columns.unit: The published unit, from the vocabulary (e.g. GJ, MW, short_ton, m3).
columns.value_canonical: The value converted to one unit per dimension (MWh, MW, MWth, t, m3, m3/day, ha, h). Empty where the unit has no fixed conversion.
columns.value_as_published: The figure exactly as written in the text it was taken from: the document's line or cell, or for registry figures the entry's own sentence.
columns.qualifier: Read from the words around the figure ('about', 'at least', 'up to').
columns.period_start: First day the figure covers (ISO date). Empty if the source gives no period.
columns.basis: What kind of document the figure rests on (metered, permitted, filed, company_statement, press_report, derived...).
columns.side: record: a regulator, court, grid operator, utility, statistics office, auditor, registry or government decision. claim: what a company, applicant or government says or plans.
columns.source_title: Title of the document, with page or table where known.
columns.source_date: Date of the document as known (ISO date, year-month or year). Empty if not known.
columns.feed: The file in this repository the row was built from. To correct a figure, edit that file and run ./rebuild.sh.
columns.extraction: How the figure was taken from its source.
columns.second_read: yes if a second reading, by a different method or person, confirmed it against the document.
columns.notes: What a reader needs to know to use the figure: caveats, conversions, part years.

site_register.description: Every site the ledger has figures or links for: datacenters, buildings that file as datacenters, crypto mining sites, nuclear plants, chip fabs, smelters and refiners. One page each on the website.

columns.site_id: Stable id. Retired ids are mapped in site_id_aliases.csv.
columns.name: Name as the register or document gives it.
columns.lat: Latitude, WGS84 decimal degrees. Empty if the site is not yet placed.
columns.status: Usually operating, permitted, under_construction, announced or refused; Texas rows carry the TCEQ project status as text.
columns.ct_source_id: Climate TRACE asset id, where the site was matched to one.
columns.backlog_id: Id in the unlocated-site backlog, if the site came from it.
columns.register_source: The register or document the site was taken from.
columns.also_known_as: Other names and ids (registration numbers, licence numbers).

entries.description: The ledger's entries as a flat table, built from registry/*.json: the record, the claim and the one-line gap between them.

columns.registry_file: The registry file the entry lives in; edit it there.
columns.country: Country or countries, as names; 'EU' and 'Global' for entries above country level.
columns.lat: Latitude of the site or area (approximate for areas).
columns.record: What the public record says, with numbers and dates.
columns.claim: What the operator or government says in public, or 'none found'.
columns.gap: The difference between record and claim, in one line, without adjectives.
columns.confidence: How firmly the record rests on record holders' documents that were read.
columns.verification_status: Result of the second reading of the record against its documents.
columns.verification_note: What was read, when, and what was found.
columns.last_checked: Date the entry was last checked.
columns.receipt: Id of the worked case in receipts/, if the entry has one.
columns.n_record_sources: Number of record sources (listed in entry_sources.csv).

entry_sources.description: Every document an entry cites, one row each, with the side it supports.

columns.side: Whether the document supports the record or the claim.
columns.title: Title, with page or section where given.
columns.date_note: Why the date is uncertain, where it is.

entity_register.description: Organisations: companies, utilities, public bodies and registers that sites, figures or chain links refer to. Which names in the ledger's sources refer to which organisation is in sites/organisations/.

columns.name: Name.
columns.kind: Company, municipal utility, cooperative, public body, joint venture, register...
columns.country: Where the organisation is registered or headquartered, where a document read gives it; empty otherwise (never inferred from where its sites are).

edges.description: Documented links in the chain from smelter to chipmaker to site and its power, fuel and water. Column guide: sites/chain/README.md.

columns.edge_id: Content hash of the row (notes and second_read excluded).
columns.leg: Which leg of the chain (refiner_to_maker, power_to_site, water_to_site...).
columns.from_type: site, entity, entry, or named (a party not yet in a register).
columns.from_name: Its name as the document gives it.
columns.relation: From the vocabulary: refines_for, supplies_power_to, supplies_water_to...
columns.to_name: Its name as the document gives it.
columns.period_start: When the link held, if the document says.
columns.basis: Kind of document; company_statement makes the edge a claim.
columns.quoted_line: The phrase in the document that states the link, copied exactly.
columns.entry_id: The ledger entry that discusses it.
columns.notes: What the reader needs to know.
columns.second_read: yes or no, with how it was confirmed.
